brief.notification_title: AI rout plus hot core PCE: VIX 35, bonds the hedge
brief.market_summary: At 10:00 ET Wednesday, US stocks are falling hard. Hot inflation and strong growth data have locked in a December Fed hike, and AI and chip stocks have resumed their slide. The S&P 500 is at 7,048.89 (-2.1%), the Nasdaq -3.1%, SMH -5.0% and the VIX 34.95. Treasuries are rallying as the safe haven anyway: the 10Y is 4.816% (-8.8bp) and the 5Y 4.606% (-10.6bp). High-yield credit is slightly weaker. Brent data conflict (more on that in the oil section), with Houthi and Hormuz risks pulling against the OPEC+ surplus worry. Bitcoin is below $58K after a sixth straight day of spot ETF outflows. Thursday's Thanksgiving closure and a likely shortened Friday mean thin trading into the weekend.
brief.since_last:
1) October PCE: core +0.3% m/m, 3.3% y/y against 3.2% expected, the fastest since late 2023. Headline was 3.8% y/y, in line. Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% from 3.4% (consensus 3.5%), and jobless claims came in at 189K against about 200K. Headlines now treat a December hike as locked (n37, n68). Yardeni is arguing for 50bp (n6).
2) The AI sell-off is back. Nvidia is down about 5-8% after Monday's Huang-reinstatement spike faded on regulatory worries (n73, n87). Anthropic is trading below its IPO price (n14). Dell beat EPS by 40% and still fell more than 4% (n13).
3) The US proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU (n66).
4) Despite the hot data, the 10Y fell about 9bp and the 5Y about 11bp. The haven bid outweighed inflation.
5) Oil: the Houthis claimed a strike on Ras Tanura (n60) and Iran reported tankers hitting mines in Hormuz (n162). Against that, Iraq and Kazakhstan want higher OPEC+ capacity estimates before the 29 Nov meeting (n24, n28).
6) BTC broke $58K. November spot BTC ETF outflows are a record $4.7-4.9bn.

economic_data.takeaway: The y/y rate is hot and the fastest since late 2023. The m/m print met the 0.3% condition from my IEF tranche-2 rule. It cements a December hike and keeps 2027 hikes in play. The front end stays firm, but the long end rallied today because the equity rout dominated.
In line. Energy is still feeding through (n3, n1). It isn't a surprise, but it gives the Fed no reason to pause.
The fastest growth in three years (n9). Growth this strong leaves the Fed free to hike into the equity sell-off, so don't count on a 'Fed put'.
A tight labor market, which also argues for higher rates. Today the bond market ignored it in favor of the haven bid. That is a warning that the rally depends on stocks staying weak.
Softer than either consensus. It is the only soft print in this morning's batch and too small to change the Fed outlook.

economic_data.when: 10:00 ET (the calendar dates it Wed; it may be Tuesday's release)
economic_data.takeaway: A big beat that adds to the strong-economy, hawkish-Fed picture. Holiday spending stories point to value-seeking (n3, n31), which fits Dollar Tree's strength.
Still expanding but cooling. The composite came in at 54.6 against 55.6 expected, and the Chicago Fed index at -0.06 against 0.20. These are the few signs of slowing growth.

A 0.3bp tail with bid-to-cover of 2.37 (research, not confirmed): adequate but soft. The 52-week bill cleared at 4.365% against 3.980% last time, a sign the market is pricing more hikes at the front end.
This is the gate for IEF tranche 2. After a 25bp weekly rally, a tail would give a better entry. A strong result would confirm haven demand.
The last major Fed release before the 8-9 Dec FOMC. Watch for wage and price language. A tariff pass-through narrative would push expectations toward a second hike in 2027.
The API build was smaller than expected, which mildly supports crude. EIA matters less than Sunday's OPEC+ meeting.
The last labor-market check before the 9 Dec FOMC. Another strong print would raise the odds of a 50bp hike.

earnings.result: EPS $9.16 vs $6.55 est (+39.9%). Record revenue of $54.9bn, and the full-year sales target was raised for the third time this year. Shares rose 2-4% after hours, then fell more than 4% pre-market.
earnings.takeaway: A 40% beat was sold. Earnings aren't the problem; positioning and doubts about how long AI capex lasts are. Dell's note that its backlog is vetted for customers' access to capital, land and power (n13) tells you what worries investors. This supports staying out of semis: don't treat a beat as a buy signal while good news still gets sold.

earnings.takeaway: Large agriculture is still weak, and the guidance midpoint is roughly flat on FY26. It adds mild pressure on industrials (XLI -1.6%) but isn't an index driver.

earnings.takeaway: Software is being sold on worries about AI disrupting it. Autodesk falling 4-5% despite a beat and raise, and Nutanix falling 8-9% on its guidance (n65), confirm the pattern. Guidance matters more than the quarter.

sections.summary: The AI unwind resumed on hot inflation, a locked-in December hike and the proposed tariffs on 14 partners. Beats from Dell, Autodesk and HP were sold. Defensives (staples, utilities, energy) are roughly flat, while tech and semis take the losses.
key_points: S&P 500 7,048.89 (-2.1%, -8.7% over a month). Nasdaq 23,003.95 (-3.1%, -13.1% over a month). The Dow is holding up better at -1.4%. Headlines had the S&P down as much as 2.8% just after the open (n5), so it has already bounced off the lows.
SMH 405.44 (-5.0%, -27.3% over a month) is close to the 400 level that extends my avoid. Nvidia is down about 5-8% after Monday's +31% Huang spike (n38, n73).
VIX 34.95 (+32.6%). Thin Thanksgiving trading (closed Thursday, likely early close Friday) can make moves in either direction bigger.
Pre-market laggards included Deere (miss), Workday (guidance), Nutanix (-8-9%) and Urban Outfitters (-10%). Dollar Tree is at a 52-week high.

sections.summary: Treasuries rallied as the haven despite hot core PCE and a GDP revision to 4.3%. The belly led, with the 5Y down 10.6bp against the 30Y down 6.1bp. The Fed outlook got more hawkish, which keeps bills and the front end yielding above 4.1%. High-yield credit is softening.
key_points: 10Y 4.816% (-8.8bp, -25bp on the week). 5Y 4.606%. 30Y 5.231%. The official 11/24 curve had the 10Y at 4.91% and 2s10s at +28bp.
IEF 92.24 (+0.65%) and TLT +1.05%. IEF tranche 1, bought near 91.64, is working as an equity hedge.
LQD +0.40% but HYG -0.23%: duration is winning while high-yield spreads leak wider, a classic risk-off split.
The 52-week bill auction yield jumped to 4.365% from 3.980%, so hikes are being priced further out. The 7-year auction and the Beige Book come today.

sections.summary: Oil is caught between attacks in the Gulf and the OPEC+ 2027 surplus worry. The price data conflict: BZ=F shows $89.77 (-1.8%), but BNO is +2.0%, WTI +1.3%, and research had January Brent at $92.41 (+1.1%) at 13:05 GMT. My guess is the BZ=F series rolled to a lower-priced later contract, so I'd trust BNO and WTI for direction. I'd stay out until after Sunday's meeting, which is binary.
key_points: Brent is about 21% below its late-October peak above $115. It dipped to about $90 in Asian hours, then rebounded on the Houthis' Ras Tanura claim (n60, n78) and Iran's report of tankers hitting mines in Hormuz (n162).
Iraq and Kazakhstan want higher capacity estimates before the 29 Nov OPEC+ meeting (n24, n28). Higher baselines mean higher 2027 quotas and a bigger surplus.
The API crude build was +126K bbl against expectations of +0.9M to +2.1M, mildly supportive. ING says Gulf exports are recovering, but Hormuz risks remain.
XLE is +0.3%, while Norse Atlantic's -78% on fuel costs (n25) shows the demand-side damage.

sections.summary: Crypto is trading like leveraged Nasdaq, not like a hedge. BTC is below $58K after the PCE print, with six straight days of spot ETF outflows and a record month of outflows. ETH and DeFi are falling about twice as fast as BTC (n128).
key_points: BTC $57,967 (-3.9%, -27% over a month), on track for its worst month since July 2022 (n110). ETH $1,639 (-3.1%). SOL $67.19. XRP $0.9027. ADA, SUI and TON are each down 4-6%.

The Coinbase premium has been negative for 60 days (n118), a sign of weak US demand. Bit Digital sold 29,825 ETH to pay down debt (n82).
Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade slipped to 2027. Developers decide 26 Nov on the next test.

brief.instructor_take: I'd focus on one thing today. The data say the economy is running hot: GDP of 4.3%, core PCE at 3.3%, claims at 189K. The Fed will hike into an equity sell-off, so there is no rescue coming before 9 December. The crowd sees the 10Y down 9bp and reads it as the bond market calling a slowdown. I read it as fear money parking in duration, and that money leaves as soon as stocks stabilize, because the inflation numbers argue for higher yields, not lower. That's why I'm adding IEF as a hedge in measured steps with a hard stop, not making it a big macro bet. In equities, the most useful signal this week is Dell: a 40% EPS beat sold off. When markets punish good news, valuations are compressing, and you can't time the bottom from fundamentals. You wait for price to stop going down on good news. A VIX near 35 often comes close to a washout, but thin holiday trading on Wednesday and Friday is the worst time to try catching a falling knife, and the tariff headlines (n66) won't be resolved by Monday. Crypto is failing as a hedge. Persistent ETF outflows are the cleanest read on demand, and they haven't turned yet. So I'm positioned this way: bills as the core, a partial Treasury hedge, no new semis or crypto, and a shopping list written down in advance so I'm buying on levels and not on emotion.

top_ideas.title: Keep T-bills as the core while the Fed hikes
top_ideas.one_liner: Hike locked after hot PCE: keep idle cash earning ~4.1% in SGOV
top_ideas.thesis: Core PCE at 3.3% y/y, GDP at 4.3% and claims at 189K make a December hike close to certain, and the 52-week bill auction shows hikes priced into 2027. Bills pay over 4.1% with almost no price risk, and that cash funds the IEF tranche and any later rebuild of semis or crypto.
top_ideas.reasoning: I'm applying the idea of option value. When volatility is high and good news gets sold, cash that earns a real yield is a position, not idleness. The 13-week yield is 4.145%. Tuesday's 3-month auction cleared at 4.180%, and the 52-week jumped to 4.365% from 3.980%, so as long as the Fed keeps hiking, the bill yield moves with it. Today's data removed any doubt about December: the Fed has a 4.3% GDP print as cover to keep going. I prefer SGOV to longer bonds for the core because it has essentially no duration risk if the haven bid fades and inflation reasserts. A less experienced investor sees 'only 4%' while the S&P is down 8.7% over a month. Avoiding that drawdown and keeping dry powder is the return. I'd change my mind if the 13-week yield fell below 4.0% or the Fed signalled that December is the last hike, because then locking in duration beats rolling bills.
risks: A fast Fed pivot (for example, if the equity sell-off turns into a credit event) would lower bill yields, and SGOV would underperform duration
Opportunity cost if equities rebound sharply from a VIX-35 washout
top_ideas.entry: Keep the existing position. Sweep idle cash into SGOV at market today, setting aside about 1.5% for IEF tranche 2 after the 7-year auction.
top_ideas.invalidation: The 13-week yield (now 4.145%) falls below 4.0%, or Fed communication signals December is the final hike or a pause.
top_ideas.sizing: The core cash sleeve: everything not committed to IEF tranche 2 and the SMH rebuild budget.

top_ideas.title: Stay out of semis: a 40% Dell beat got sold
top_ideas.one_liner: Dell beat by 40% and fell: no semis buying until SMH reclaims 445
top_ideas.thesis: SMH is down 27% in a month and 5% today, near the 400 level. Beats from Dell, ADI and HP aren't lifting the group, and the Nvidia governance and regulatory overhang plus the China tariff proposal add new risk. Wait for price confirmation, not a story.
top_ideas.reasoning: The concept here is price reaction to news. When a 40% EPS beat and a third guidance raise produce a 4% drop, the market is telling you the marginal buyer is gone. Valuations are compressing faster than earnings are rising. Nvidia rose 31% on Monday and gave it all back within two sessions, which shows how violent the swings are in both directions. That volatility is exactly why I want a rule, not a guess. I chose 'avoid' over buying a cheaper chip name because the drivers today are sector-wide: tariffs on China (n66), regulatory costs for the whole AI industry (n73) and a December hike pushing up discount rates. What a less experienced investor can miss: Friday's likely half-day session doesn't count as a full-session close, so a holiday-thin pop to 445 shouldn't trigger anything. What would prove me wrong is two full-session closes above 445, which would mean buyers are absorbing the bad news.
catalysts: Progress on the tariff proposal for 14 partners (n66)
risks: A short-covering V-bottom from VIX 35 runs away without me
Trump pardon or regulatory relief headlines spark a squeeze like Monday's +31% Nvidia move
top_ideas.entry: No semis buying today or in Friday's thin session. Trigger unchanged: after two consecutive full-session closes above 445, buy half of the previously trimmed amount from SGOV, and the second half after another week above 445.
top_ideas.invalidation: Two full-session closes above 445 end the avoid. A close below 400 (now 405.44) extends it through the 9 Dec FOMC.
top_ideas.sizing: 0% new. If you still hold a core semis position, don't add to it, and don't panic-sell it into today's low either.

top_ideas.title: IEF tranche 2: hedge is working, add after 7Y auction
top_ideas.one_liner: Core PCE 0.3% m/m met the rule: add IEF tranche 2 after the 7Y sale
top_ideas.thesis: Tuesday's tranche 1, bought near 91.64, is up about 0.65% as the 10Y fell to 4.816% during the equity rout, so the hedge is doing its job. Core PCE printed 0.3% m/m, which meets the tranche-2 condition. But the y/y rate is hot, so I'll take the rest only after the 7-year auction and under a firm stop.
top_ideas.reasoning: The concept is the conditional stock-bond correlation. Treasuries hedge equities when the shock is about risk or growth, not when it's about inflation. Today's shock is the AI and tariff sell-off, so bonds rallied even though core PCE hit 3.3%. That's what I bought tranche 1 for. My pre-set rule said to add if core PCE was 0.3% m/m or less. It was, and I follow rules I set before the data, with one execution refinement. The 10Y has already fallen 25bp this week, and $44bn of 7-year supply comes today, so I let the auction pass and look for a tail to give a better price. I chose IEF over TLT because 7-10Y duration hedges well without the 30Y's exposure to term premium and supply at 5.23%. What a less experienced investor misses is that this rally depends on stocks staying weak: GDP, claims and core inflation all argue for higher yields once fear fades. That's why the stop stays at a 10Y close above 5.15%, and I won't chase below 4.75%.
risks: Equities stabilize and the haven bid reverses while the inflation data push yields higher (stocks and bonds falling together, as in 2022)
A 50bp December hike or hawkish dots
Weak 7-year demand or more tariff-driven inflation fears
top_ideas.entry: Tranche 1 (1.5%): hold if filled near 91.64. Tranche 2 (1.5%): buy at market after the 7-year auction result, provided the 10Y is between 4.75% and 4.90% (now 4.816%). If the 10Y is below 4.75%, wait for 4.85%. If you missed tranche 1, don't add it now; the 10Y is below the 4.85% rule, so wait for a backup to 4.90%. Fund from SGOV.
top_ideas.invalidation: A 10Y close above 5.15% exits the whole position.
top_ideas.sizing: 3% total (1.5% + 1.5%) as an equity hedge. No more until after the 9 Dec FOMC.

brief.prior_ideas_review:
1) ADD SGOV worked as intended. The 13-week yield is 4.145% (4.168% yesterday), far above the 4.0% invalidation, and today's data lock in December (n37, n68). Keep it.
2) AVOID SMH was right. Dell's beat didn't lift the open: DELL fell more than 4%, and SMH is at 405.44 (-5.0% today, -11.8% on the week), nowhere near the 445 trigger and close to the 400 extension level. Keep it, with the same rules.
3) BUY IEF: tranche 1, bought near 91.64 with the 10Y at 4.904%, is now 92.24 (+0.65%), with the 10Y at 4.816%. It hedged the equity drop as planned. The tranche-2 condition was met (core PCE +0.3% m/m), so I'm executing it after the 7-year auction, with a no-chase floor of 4.75% on the 10Y. If you missed tranche 1, don't chase it: the 10Y is below the 4.85% rule. Keep it, with this adjustment.

lesson.concept: The stock-bond correlation depends on the type of shock
lesson.explanation: High-quality government bonds hedge stocks only when the shock hitting stocks is about growth or fear. Then investors run to safety, yields fall and bond prices rise. When the shock is inflation, both can fall together, as in 2022, because higher inflation means higher rates, which hurts both. So a Treasury hedge isn't automatic: you have to ask which force is driving the market each day and size the hedge for the day the other force wins.
lesson.todays_example: By the textbook, core PCE at 3.3% y/y (above the 3.2% consensus), GDP revised to 4.3% and claims at 189K should have sent yields up. Instead the 10Y fell 8.8bp to 4.816% and TLT rose 1.05%, because the Nasdaq's 3% drop and a VIX of 35 drove the market. IEF tranche 1 gained about 0.65% while SMH lost 5%. The inflation data are still there, though, which is why the IEF idea keeps a 5.15% stop.
